title: Sounding natural
goal: React like a local, use tag questions and emphasis particles, make echo words, ask people to repeat or explain, get round words you don't know, and mix in English the way people do.
intro:
You can now say almost anything in correct Gujarati. This unit is about saying it the way Gujaratis do: the little noises (**હાશ!**, **બાપ રે!**, **અરેરે!**), the tags that turn a statement into a friendly question (**મસ્ત છે, નહીં?**, **તું આવે છે ને?**), the particles **જ**, **તો**, **ય** and **વળી** that carry so much of the meaning, and echo words like **ચા-બા** 'tea or something'.

You'll also practise the survival skills of a learner: asking people to repeat or slow down, asking what a word means, describing a thing whose name you've forgotten, and mixing in English — because every Gujarati you meet does.

grammar.title: Tag questions: ને?, નહીં?, ખરું?, કે શું?
grammar.body:
Gujarati turns a statement into a friendly 'isn't it? / right?' question with a small word at the end and a rising voice.

**ને?** — the everyday tag, expecting 'yes': **તું આવે છે ને?** 'you're coming, aren't you?', **ખબર છે ને?** 'you know, right?'
**નહીં?** — after a positive opinion, inviting agreement: **મસ્ત છે, નહીં?** 'it's great, isn't it?'
**ખરું? / ખરું ને?** — 'right? / am I right?': **આ રસ્તો સાચો છે, ખરું ને?** It never changes for gender.
**કે શું?** — 'or what?', teasing or impatient: **સૂઈ ગયો કે શું?** 'have you fallen asleep or what?'
**હં?** — after a request or instruction, 'OK?': **મોડું નહીં કરતો, હં?**

**Answering**: **હા ને!** 'yes, of course! / tell me about it!' agrees warmly; **ના રે!** 'oh no, not at all!' denies softly.

The trap: a final **ને** is not **ના** 'no'. **તું આવે છે ને?** expects *yes*. And after a command **ને** coaxes rather than asks: **બેસો ને** 'do sit down'.

examples.roman: tuṃ pāgal thaī gayo ke shuṃ?
examples.en: Have you gone mad or what?

grammar.title: Emphasis: જ, તો, ય, વળી, થોડું
grammar.body:
Gujarati puts emphasis on a word by adding a small particle **right after it**. Moving the particle moves the meaning.

**જ** 'exactly, only, the very': **આજે જ** 'today itself', **એ જ** 'the same one', **મેં જ કહ્યું** '*I'm* the one who said it'. Compare **હું જ જઈશ** 'I'll be the one to go' and **હું આજે જ જઈશ** 'I'll go today itself'.

**તો** 'as for, at least' (contrast): **મને તો ગમ્યું** 'well, *I* liked it'. It also softens a command (**જો તો!** 'just look!') and opens a reply (**તો?** 'so?').

**ય** (casual **પણ**) 'too, even': **હું ય આવું છું** 'I'm coming too'.

**વળી** 'now, on top of that' — annoyed or surprised: **આ વળી કોણ છે?** 'and who's this now?', **આજે વળી શું થયું?** 'what's happened now?'

**થોડું** in a question means 'hardly': **એમ થોડું ચાલે?** 'that's hardly OK, is it?' = 'that won't do'.

The trap: these particles come **after** the word they stress, never before: ~~જ આજે~~.

grammar.title: Echo words and doubled words: ચા-બા, ધીમે ધીમે
grammar.body:
**Echo words** make a word vaguer and friendlier: 'X or something, X and stuff'. Repeat the word with its first consonant replaced by **બ**: **ચા-બા** 'tea or something', **નાસ્તો-બાસ્તો** 'a snack or whatever', **પાણી-બાણી** 'water or anything'. If the word already starts with બ, use **વ**: **બિસ્કિટ-વિસ્કિટ**. Echo words are warm and casual — perfect for offering things to guests and friends, odd in a job interview.

**Doubled words** have several jobs:
- gradually / intensity: **ધીમે ધીમે** 'slowly, bit by bit', **ગરમ ગરમ** 'piping hot', **ફટાફટ** 'in a flash'
- 'which all, who all' (expecting a list): **ક્યાં ક્યાં ગયા?** 'where all did you go?', **કોણ કોણ આવ્યું?** 'who all came?', **શું શું ખાધું?** 'what all did you eat?'
- ongoing action: **-તાં -તાં** 'while …-ing': **વાત કરતાં કરતાં** 'while chatting'; **-ઈ -ઈને** 'repeatedly': **અટકી અટકીને** 'haltingly'

The trap: in **ક્યાં ક્યાં / કોણ કોણ** the verb agrees as if with a group: **કોણ કોણ આવ્યું હતું?** (neuter for a mixed group).

examples.roman: dhīme dhīme badhuṃ ṭhīk thaī jashe.
examples.en: Bit by bit everything will be fine.
What all did you eat at the wedding?

culture: Sounding natural in Gujarati is mostly about the small words. Listeners react constantly (**હં**, **હા ને!**, **બાપ રે!**), requests end with **ને** or **હં**, and **જ** and **તો** do the work English does with stress and tone of voice. Regional accents are a favourite topic: the **સુરતી** way of speaking is famously blunt and colourful (Suratis are teased for their swearing and loved for their food), and **કાઠિયાવાડી** from Saurashtra says **હાલો** for ચાલો 'let's go' and **મા** for 'don't' (**જા મા** 'don't go'). Nobody minds a learner's accent; people will happily **ટોકે** (correct) you if you ask. English is everywhere: urban Gujaratis say **ઍક્ચ્યુઅલી**, **સિરિયસલી**, **ટેન્શન**, **ઍડજસ્ટ કરવું** without thinking, and in Leicester, Wembley or New Jersey family Gujarati is full of fridge, milk and parking. If you forget a word, say it in English or describe it (**એક જાતની…**) — that is exactly what native speakers do.

tip.title: React out loud
tip.body:
- Good news: **વાહ!** · teasing surprise: **ઓહો!** · bad news: **અરેરે!** · gross: **છી!**
- Relief: **હાશ!** · shock: **બાપ રે!** · exasperation: **ભાઈસાબ!**
- **સાચ્ચે?** 'seriously?' · agree warmly: **હા ને, યાર!**

tip.title: Tags: ને?, નહીં?, ખરું?
tip.body:
- **ને?** expects yes: તું આવે છે **ને**?
- **નહીં?** after an opinion: મસ્ત છે, **નહીં**?
- **ખરું (ને)?** 'right?' — never changes.
- **કે શું?** 'or what?' · **હં?** 'OK?' after a request.
- Answer **હા ને!** or **ના રે!**

tip.title: જ, તો, ય, વળી
tip.body:
- The particle goes **right after** the word it stresses.
- **જ** 'exactly, the very': આજે **જ**, **મેં જ** કહ્યું.
- **તો** 'as for': મને **તો** ગમ્યું. **ય** 'too': હું **ય**.
- **વળી** 'now' (annoyed): આ **વળી** કોણ છે?
- **થોડું** in a question = 'hardly': એમ **થોડું** ચાલે?

tip.title: ચા-બા and ધીમે ધીમે
tip.body:
- Echo word = the word + a copy starting with **બ**: **ચા-બા** 'tea or something', **નાસ્તો-બાસ્તો**. Casual and friendly.
- Doubling: **ધીમે ધીમે** 'bit by bit', **ગરમ ગરમ** 'piping hot'.
- 'Who all, where all': **કોણ કોણ**, **ક્યાં ક્યાં**.
- 'While …-ing': **કરતાં કરતાં**.

tip.title: Asking again
tip.body:
- Stop someone: **એક મિનિટ, શું કહ્યું?**
- Again: **ફરીથી બોલ ને?** (friend) · **ફરીથી કહેશો?** (polite) · Slower: **જરા ધીમે બોલશો?**
- **સમજાવું** 'to be understood' works like ગમવું: **મને** સમજાયું / સમજાયું નહીં.
- Don't mix it up with **સમજાવવું** 'to explain': ફરીથી **સમજાવશો**?

sentences.native: એક મિનિટ, શું કહ્યું? ફરીથી બોલ ને?
sentences.roman: ek miniṭ, shuṃ kahyuṃ? farīthī bol ne?
sentences.en: Hang on, what did you say? Say it again?

sentences.native: સૉરી, જરા ધીમે બોલશો? હું હજી શીખું છું.
sentences.roman: sorī, jarā dhīme bolsho? huṃ hajī shīkhuṃ chhuṃ.
sentences.en: Sorry, could you speak a bit more slowly? I'm still learning.
I didn't get it, could you explain again?
Got it? Yes, got it perfectly.

sentences.native: એનો સુરતી લહેકો છે, એટલે થોડું અઘરું પડે છે.
sentences.roman: eno suratī laheko chhe, eṭle thoḍuṃ aghruṃ paḍe chhe.
sentences.en: He's got a Surati accent, so it's a bit hard.
Your pronunciation is really good!

sentences.native: હું હજી અટકી અટકીને બોલું છું.
sentences.roman: huṃ hajī aṭkī aṭkīne boluṃ chhuṃ.
sentences.en: I still speak haltingly.

sentences.native: વચ્ચે બોલું છું, માફ કરજો, પણ ટ્રેન કેટલા વાગ્યે છે?
sentences.roman: vachche boluṃ chhuṃ, māf karjo, paṇ ṭren keṭlā vāgye chhe?
sentences.en: Sorry to interrupt, but what time is the train?

sentences.native: એ લોકો એટલું ફટાફટ બોલે છે કે કંઈ સમજાતું નથી.
sentences.roman: e loko eṭluṃ faṭāfaṭ bole chhe ke kaṃī samjātuṃ nathī.
sentences.en: They talk so fast I can't understand a thing.
Don't stop, keep talking! (to a man)

lessons.title: When you don't know the word

tip.title: Getting round a missing word
tip.body:
- Ask: **આને ગુજરાતીમાં શું કહેવાય?** · Stall: **શું કહેવાય… પેલું…**
- Describe it: **એક જાતની મીઠાઈ છે** 'it's a kind of sweet' (**જાતનો / જાતની / જાતનું** agrees).
- Or just use English with **કરવું / થવું** — everyone does: **મિક્સ કરવું**, **ટેન્શન થવું**.

sentences.native: આને ગુજરાતીમાં શું કહેવાય? મને શબ્દ યાદ નથી.
sentences.roman: āne gujarātīmāṃ shuṃ kahevāy? mane shabd yād nathī.
sentences.en: What do you call this in Gujarati? I can't remember the word.

sentences.native: શું કહેવાય… પેલું… જેમાં ચા બનાવીએ!
sentences.roman: shuṃ kahevāy… peluṃ… jemāṃ chā banāvīe!
sentences.en: What's it called… that thing… you make tea in!
"Jalso" — what does that mean?

sentences.native: આ એક જાતની મીઠાઈ છે, દૂધમાંથી બને છે.
sentences.roman: ā ek jātnī mīṭhāī chhe, dūdhmāṃthī bane chhe.
sentences.en: It's a kind of sweet, it's made from milk.
Dhokla is a kind of snack.

sentences.native: ઍક્ચ્યુઅલી, મને ખબર નહોતી કે આજે રજા છે.
sentences.roman: ekchyuālī, mane khabar nahotī ke āje rajā chhe.
sentences.en: Actually, I didn't know today was a holiday.

sentences.native: અમે ઘરે ગુજલિશ જ બોલીએ છીએ.
sentences.roman: ame ghare gujlish j bolīe chhīe.
sentences.en: At home we just speak Gujlish.

sentences.native: આ શબ્દનો અર્થ મને સમજાવ ને.
sentences.roman: ā shabdno arth mane samjāv ne.
sentences.en: Go on, explain to me what this word means.

sentences.native: મારી ભૂલ થાય તો ટોકજે, હં!
sentences.roman: mārī bhūl thāy to ṭokje, haṃ!
sentences.en: If I make a mistake, correct me, OK?

sentences.native: એ ગુજરાતીમાં ઘણા અંગ્રેજી શબ્દો મિક્સ કરે છે.
sentences.roman: e gujarātīmāṃ ghaṇā aṅgrejī shabdo miks kare chhe.
sentences.en: He mixes lots of English words into his Gujarati.
